cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light services model with a dual execution framework rather than owned manufacturing. Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors while design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; all subcontractors are directly hired and managed by the Company and all subcontracted work is carried out under its active guidance and on-ground supervision, with supervisors physically present on-site for the full duration of the project. Both partial and full subcontracting models are used, and the Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. The outsourcing model runs a formal two-step process (vendor screening - define project requirements, identify potential vendors, pre-screening checklist covering GST/PAN and financial stability, RFP/RFQ, proposal evaluation, vendor interviews, due diligence and background checks including litigation/blacklisting, final selection and contracting, onboarding and governance; then project execution - project management tools, milestone work plan, daily status calls and on-site monitoring, final delivery and handover). The in-house model covers material requirement definition (plywood, commercial ply, nylon carpet rolls and other construction/finish items), vendor shortlisting, RFQ, quotation evaluation, purchase order issue, material delivery and inspection, payment processing and inventory recordkeeping. Revenue by execution mode (% of total revenue): Subcontract 90.89% / 92.11% / 75.48% / 64.40% and In-house 9.11% / 7.89% / 24.52% / 35.60% for the period ended Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23. Vendor and execution metrics (not cumulative), Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23: total active subcontractors globally (domestic and international) 53 / 36 / 29 / 22; projects executed with international local allies 125 / 69 / 49 / 20; projects executed domestically 307 / 312 / 207 / 205; total booths delivered globally 432 / 381 / 256 / 225; total repeat clients 63 / 27 / 28 / 48; average project turnaround time 3 to 30 days in every period. The Company states it does not own fabrication machinery or permanent event spaces and instead rents godowns, fabrication equipment, raw materials and temporary project sites project-by-project; materials are sourced locally in overseas markets to reduce logistics dependencies. Risk factors disclose that there are no executed registered formal arrangements with the outsourced subcontractors governing specifications, quality standards, sales estimates or packaging, and that foreign outsourcing adds FX, cross-border regulatory, geopolitical and logistical exposure. Registered office and both godowns are on leasehold premises. International client base grew 245% over the last three years, from 20 to 69 international clients; total booths delivered globally grew at a stated CAGR of 30.13% from FY23 to FY25.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- These three states contributed Rs. 3,556.30 lakhs / 68.21% of domestic revenue for the period ended February 28, 2026 (FY25: 74.79%; FY24: 80.44%; FY23: 85.40%). Operations are susceptible to local and regional factors - economic and weather conditions, natural disasters, demographic changes - and to social, political or economic disruption, natural calamities, civil disruption, changes in state/local/central government policy or adverse competitive developments in those states. The Company states it has not experienced such an adverse impact as of the period ended February 28, 2026 or in the last three Fiscals, but gives no assurance for the future.
- Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced. The Company states it does not have any executed registered formal arrangements with such outsourced subcontractors governing matters such as specification of products, quality standards to be maintained, sales estimates and packaging of products. The risk factor text is truncated mid-sentence in the routed extract.
- All industry and market information in the Business and Risk Factors sections is derived from the Dun & Bradstreet Report, which was commissioned by and paid for by the Company for the purpose of the Offer - a stated conflict/reliance caveat.
- The DRHP states that various operational performance indicators may not be derived from the Restated Financial Statements, may not have been subjected to audit or review by the Statutory Auditor, and that their calculation method may vary from that used by other companies; investors are cautioned against undue reliance.
- Promoters hold 1,06,75,996 Equity Shares constituting 94.55% of the pre-Offer issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital, and both Promoters are also selling shareholders in the Offer for Sale (up to 8,00,000 shares combined). Stated as fact in the Promoters and Objects sections; the DRHP text provided does not present this as a numbered risk factor.
